Plot out-of-fold model performance

Source: R/plot_performance.R
plot_performance.Rd

Creates performance plots for models evaluated by `find_bestfit()`. For non-binary outcomes, the default is an observed-versus-predicted plot. For binomial outcomes, the default is a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.

Usage

plot_performance(
  object,
  model_id = NULL,
  metrics = "CCC",
  type = c("auto", "observed_predicted", "roc", "threshold", "confusion"),
  threshold = NULL,
  x = "observed",
  y = "predicted",
  scale_factor = 1,
  ncol = NULL,
  metric_digits = 2L,
  x_lab = NULL,
  y_lab = NULL,
  show_fit = TRUE,
  fit_se = FALSE,
  fit_color = "orange",
  show_identity = TRUE,
  identity_color = "red",
  identity_linetype = "dashed",
  label_x = -Inf,
  label_y = Inf,
  label_hjust = -0.1,
  label_vjust = 1.2,
  label_size = 3.5,
  base_size = 11,
  point_args = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A non-empty data frame returned by `find_bestfit()`. It must contain a unique `model_id` column, the requested metric columns, and retained out-of-fold predictions.

model_id

Optional vector of model identifiers to plot. If `NULL`, every retained model with available predictions is plotted.

metrics

Unique character vector naming validation metrics stored as numeric columns of `object`. Metrics are displayed in the supplied order. Common non-binary metrics include `"CCC"`, `"Cb"`, `"rho"`, `"RMSE"`, and `"MAE"`. Binomial metrics include `"ROC_AUC"`, `"Brier"`, `"LogLoss"`, `"Accuracy"`, `"Balanced_Accuracy"`, `"Sensitivity"`, `"Specificity"`, `"Precision"`, `"F1"`, and `"MCC"`.

type

Character. Plot type selected from `"auto"`, `"observed_predicted"`, `"roc"`, `"threshold"`, or `"confusion"`. `"auto"` uses an ROC curve for binomial outcomes and an observed-versus-predicted plot otherwise.

threshold

Optional probability threshold strictly between 0 and 1. If `NULL`, `attr(object, "threshold")` is used when available; otherwise `0.5` is used. It is used by `"threshold"` and `"confusion"` plots and identifies the selected operating point on ROC curves.

x

Character scalar naming the observed-value column in prediction data. Default is `"observed"`.

y

Character scalar naming the predicted-value column in prediction data. For binomial outcomes, this column must contain probabilities in `[0, 1]`. Default is `"predicted"`.

scale_factor

Finite non-zero numeric scalar multiplying both axes only for `type = "observed_predicted"`. Use `100` to display proportions as percentages.

ncol

Optional positive integer passed to `ggplot2::facet_wrap()`.

metric_digits

Non-negative integer controlling metric-label precision.

x_lab, y_lab

Optional axis labels. Plot-type-specific labels are used when either argument is `NULL`.

show_fit

Logical. For observed-versus-predicted plots, add a linear fitted line.

fit_se

Logical. Display an uncertainty band around the fitted line.

fit_color

Color of the fitted regression line.

show_identity

Logical. For observed-versus-predicted plots, add the 1:1 line. For ROC curves, add the no-discrimination diagonal.

identity_color

Color of the identity or no-discrimination line.

identity_linetype

Line type of the identity or no-discrimination line.

label_x, label_y

Numeric positions for metric labels. Infinite defaults place labels close to a panel corner where supported.

label_hjust, label_vjust

Horizontal and vertical justification for metric labels.

label_size

Numeric text size for metric labels and confusion-matrix counts.

base_size

Base font size passed to `ggplot2::theme_bw()`.

point_args

Optional named list of additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::geom_point()` for observed-versus-predicted plots.

...

Additional named arguments passed to `ggplot2::geom_point()` for observed-versus-predicted plots.

Value

A `ggplot` object that can be extended with additional ggplot2 layers, scales, labels, or themes.

Details

The function retrieves out-of-fold predictions from the `"predictions_by_model"` attribute, or from the `"predictions"` attribute when the model-specific list is unavailable. Model-level validation metrics are retrieved from columns of the main `find_bestfit()` result.

`plot_performance()` does not refit models or recalculate their stored validation metrics. Predictions are obtained from:

`attr(object, "predictions_by_model")`

or, when that list is unavailable:

`attr(object, "predictions")`

For binomial outcomes, ROC curves are reconstructed directly from the observed classes and out-of-fold predicted probabilities. Sensitivity and specificity are calculated over the distinct probability thresholds represented in the selected predictions.

The ROC curve uses false-positive rate (`1 - specificity`) on the x-axis and sensitivity on the y-axis. A highlighted point identifies performance at `threshold`.

Threshold plots display sensitivity and specificity across probability thresholds and add a vertical line at the selected threshold.

Confusion matrices classify probabilities using `predicted >= threshold` and report classification counts.

The ROC and threshold plots require both observed classes. The observed values must be coded as `0` and `1`, and predicted values must be finite probabilities in `[0, 1]`.

Examples

performance_results <- data.frame(
  model_id = c("model_1", "model_2"),
  CCC = c(0.91, 0.86),
  Cb = c(0.96, 0.93),
  rho = c(0.95, 0.92),
  RMSE = c(0.07, 0.10),
  MAE = c(0.05, 0.08)
)

continuous_predictions <- list(
  model_1 = data.frame(
    observed = c(0.05, 0.12, 0.20, 0.31, 0.43, 0.55),
    predicted = c(0.06, 0.14, 0.18, 0.29, 0.46, 0.53)
  ),
  model_2 = data.frame(
    observed = c(0.05, 0.12, 0.20, 0.31, 0.43, 0.55),
    predicted = c(0.09, 0.16, 0.24, 0.27, 0.39, 0.49)
  )
)

attr(
  performance_results,
  "predictions_by_model"
) <- continuous_predictions

continuous_plot <- plot_performance(
  performance_results,
  metrics = c("CCC", "Cb", "rho"),
  scale_factor = 100,
  x_lab = "Observed (%)",
  y_lab = "Predicted (%)",
  size = 2.5,
  alpha = 0.8
)

binary_results <- data.frame(
  model_id = c("model_1", "model_2"),
  ROC_AUC = c(0.88, 0.82),
  Brier = c(0.14, 0.18)
)

binary_predictions <- list(
  model_1 = data.frame(
    observed = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1),
    predicted = c(0.08, 0.21, 0.39, 0.58, 0.77, 0.91)
  ),
  model_2 = data.frame(
    observed = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1),
    predicted = c(0.18, 0.31, 0.48, 0.52, 0.68, 0.79)
  )
)

attr(binary_results, "outcome_type") <- "binary"
attr(binary_results, "threshold") <- 0.5
attr(binary_results, "predictions_by_model") <- binary_predictions

roc_plot <- plot_performance(
  binary_results,
  metrics = c("ROC_AUC", "Brier")
)

threshold_plot <- plot_performance(
  binary_results,
  model_id = "model_1",
  metrics = "ROC_AUC",
  type = "threshold"
)

confusion_plot <- plot_performance(
  binary_results,
  model_id = "model_1",
  metrics = c("ROC_AUC", "Brier"),
  type = "confusion"
)

stopifnot(
  inherits(continuous_plot, "ggplot"),
  inherits(roc_plot, "ggplot"),
  inherits(threshold_plot, "ggplot"),
  inherits(confusion_plot, "ggplot")
)
